rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a good-quality expanded/full blastocyst with visible ICM, cohesive TE, and thinned zona; notes uncertainty between late stage 3 and early stage 4 appropriately. Minor limitation is slight overconfidence from a single image/focal plane.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, unexplained infertility, sperm parameters, endometrial thickness, and especially prior IVF failures with embryo quality to contextualize prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis tempered appropriately by prior failed cycles. Minor issue is somewhat broad probability framing and limited distinction between implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth.

Recommendations are well aligned with Gardner grading interpretation, SET preference for a good-quality day-5 blastocyst at age 35, avoidance of routine unproven add-ons, and selective consideration of uterine evaluation and PGT-A.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support review, transfer technique, uterine reassessment, embryology review, and selective male-factor/PGT-A workup.
